title: Mapping U.S. Federal AI Governance Against Sector Vulnerability
abstract: arXiv:2609.16260v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) poses different levels of risk across sectors, but are these differences reflected in U.S. federal AI governance? To help answer this question, we assess 684 federal AI governance documents for their coverage of 14 sectors and 24 AI risks. We measure coverage as breadth (i.e., how frequently the risk or sector is addressed across documents) and depth (i.e., how substantively the risk or sector is discussed). We then compare sector coverage patterns for each of the 24 risks with vulnerability assessments from a Delphi study of 272 experts. Our analysis finds substantial variation in coverage: AI risks related to robustness, system security, and governance receive more attention than socioeconomic, environmental, and emerging risks, including multi-agent risks. Public administration, national security, information, and scientific services receive comparatively high levels of coverage relative to other sectors

translated_title: 将美国联邦人工智能治理与行业脆弱性进行映射对比
translated_abstract: 摘要：人工智能（AI）在不同行业构成不同等级的风险，但这些差异是否反映在美国联邦人工智能治理中？为帮助回答这一问题，我们评估了684份联邦人工智能治理文件对14个行业和24种人工智能风险的覆盖情况。我们用广度（即该风险或行业在各文件中被提及的频率）和深度（即该风险或行业被讨论的实质性程度）来衡量覆盖程度。随后，我们将24种风险各自对应的行业覆盖模式，与一项由272名专家参与的德尔菲研究所得出的脆弱性评估进行比较。我们的分析发现覆盖程度存在显著差异：与稳健性、系统安全和治理相关的人工智能风险受到的关注多于社会经济、环境和新兴风险（包括多智能体风险）。与其他行业相比，公共管理、国家安全、信息和科学服务获得了相对较高的覆盖水平。
tldr: 该研究通过分析684份美国联邦人工智能治理文件对14个行业和24种AI风险的覆盖广度与深度，并与272名专家的脆弱性评估对比，发现治理重点集中于稳健性、系统安全等风险以及公共管理、国家安全等行业，而社会经济、环境和多智能体等新兴风险相对被忽视。
en_tdlr: By analyzing 684 U.S. federal AI governance documents' breadth and depth of coverage of 14 sectors and 24 AI risks, and comparing them with vulnerability assessments from 272 experts, this study finds that governance attention concentrates on robustness, system security, and governance risks as well as sectors like public administration and national security, while socioeconomic, environmental, and emerging risks such as multi-agent risks remain relatively overlooked.
